public_safety_ministers.name: Ralph Goodale
public_safety_ministers.notable: Public Safety Minister through the initial PRC/CCP interference period. Tabled Bill C-59 (National Security Act 2017) reforming CSIS Act. Cross-axis: also in corrections dossier (tabled Bill C-83 SIUs).

public_safety_ministers.name: Bill Blair
public_safety_ministers.notable: Public Safety Minister during the early Han Dong nomination irregularity period. Cross-axis: also in arms pipeline dossier (Defence 2023-2025) and corrections dossier.

public_safety_ministers.name: Marco Mendicino
public_safety_ministers.notable: Public Safety Minister when CSIS briefings on PRC interference were reportedly not forwarded to the PMO. Fired from cabinet July 2023 over multiple information-handling controversies.

public_safety_ministers.name: Dominic LeBlanc
public_safety_ministers.notable: Public Safety Minister who tabled Bill C-70 (Countering Foreign Interference Act, 2024). Cross-axis: also in corrections dossier.

csis_directors.name: Michel Coulombe
csis_directors.notable: CSIS Director during the early Trudeau-era expansion of foreign interference files. Briefing channels to PMO established during this tenure.

csis_directors.name: David Vigneault
csis_directors.notable: Six-year CSIS Director. Delivered the 2018 internal briefing on PRC targeting of Chinese-Canadian candidates. Reports reportedly not forwarded through the PMO national security adviser channel. Departed 2023.

csis_directors.name: Dan Rogers
csis_directors.notable: CSIS Director through the Hogue Commission proceedings (Sept 2023 through Jan 2025 final report).

pmo_security_advisors.name: Katie Telford
pmo_security_advisors.notable: Ten-year Trudeau chief of staff. CSIS briefings reached her office; question of whether they reached the PM is a central dispute in the Hogue Commission record. Testified before Parliament on the interference dossier.

pmo_security_advisors.name: Jody Thomas
pmo_security_advisors.role: National Security and Intelligence Adviser to the PM
pmo_security_advisors.notable: NSIA during the height of public foreign interference revelations (Globe and Mail reporting, March 2023). The position through which CSIS briefings reach the PM.

oversight_bodies.name: Justice Marie-Josee Hogue
oversight_bodies.notable: Quebec Court of Appeal Justice appointed to lead the Public Inquiry into Foreign Interference in Federal Electoral Processes and Democratic Institutions. Final Report delivered January 28, 2025.

oversight_bodies.name: NSICOP (Chair David McGuinty 2022-2024)
oversight_bodies.role: National Security and Intelligence Committee of Parliamentarians
oversight_bodies.notable: Tabled the June 2024 special report naming unnamed parliamentarians as 'witting or semi-witting' participants in foreign interference. McGuinty moved to Public Safety Minister 2025.

oversight_bodies.name: Nancy Belanger
oversight_bodies.notable: Lobbying Commissioner throughout the foreign interference period. Holds authority over the Registry of Lobbyists, including foreign-state-linked lobbying disclosures.

parliamentarians_implicated_or_targeted.name: Michael Chong
parliamentarians_implicated_or_targeted.notable: Long-serving CPC MP. CSIS briefing disclosed that PRC had targeted him and his family in Hong Kong. His treatment was the trigger for multiple policy reviews. Testified before Hogue Commission.

parliamentarians_implicated_or_targeted.name: Han Dong
parliamentarians_implicated_or_targeted.notable: LPC MP whose 2019 nomination was flagged by CSIS for alleged PRC interference. Expelled from caucus March 2023 after Global News reporting. Sued Global News for defamation. Later returned to Parliament as independent.

foreign_entities_grover_amplified.name: Israeli Government (network Grover M=3, 100% success)
foreign_entities_grover_amplified.role: highest-degree foreign node in influence network
foreign_entities_grover_amplified.notable: Amplified by tenet5 network Grover (foreign_any, foreign_high_degree). Degree 70.95. Connected via CIJA and multiple MP nodes labelled 'Israel support'. See data/grover_network_multi_criteria.json.

foreign_entities_grover_amplified.name: Russia / TASS (network Grover M=3)
foreign_entities_grover_amplified.notable: Amplified by tenet5 network Grover. Degree 70.27. Connected to multiple Canadian media and MP nodes. See same data file.

timeline.event: Trudeau sworn in. Ralph Goodale appointed Public Safety Minister.
Bill C-59 (National Security Act 2017) tabled — reforms CSIS Act.
Han Dong wins LPC Don Valley North nomination amid CSIS reported concerns.
Globe and Mail reports CSIS documents describing PRC interference in 2019 and 2021 elections.
Han Dong expelled from LPC caucus after Global News reporting.
Michael Chong testimony: CSIS briefing disclosed PRC targeting of him and his Hong Kong family.
Marco Mendicino fired from cabinet in shuffle.
Hogue Commission formally established. Justice Marie-Josée Hogue appointed Commissioner.
NSICOP Special Report on Foreign Interference tabled — names unnamed parliamentarians as 'witting or semi-witting' participants.
Bill C-70 (Countering Foreign Interference Act) tabled by Public Safety Minister Dominic LeBlanc.
Bill C-70 receives Royal Assent — Foreign Influence Transparency Registry, CSIS Act amendments.
Hogue Commission Final Report released. Names PRC as principal state actor; identifies structural PMO communication gaps.

NSICOP — National Security and Intelligence Committee of Parliamentarians
judicial_instruments_deployed: Public Inquiry under the Inquiries Act (Hogue Commission)
Defamation suit: Dong v Global News (ongoing)
accountability_chain.legislative_response: Bill C-70 (2024) — Foreign Influence Transparency Registry not yet fully operational
accountability_chain.result_2025: Hogue Final Report January 2025 names PRC as principal actor; recommends structural reforms to PMO briefing channels; C-70 registry implementation pending; no Canadian office-holder has been charged under any foreign-interference-related offence
